name: Obadiah
overview: Obadiah was a male descendant of the tribe of Zebulun, known primarily as the father of Ishmaiah. His mention in Scripture is brief and focused on his familial connection, without additional personal details or notable events.
namesAndTitles: The name Obadiah means 'servant [worshiper] of YHWH,' reflecting a theologically rich Hebrew name that emphasizes devotion to God. This name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 27:19.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Obadiah as a descendant of Zebulun and as the father of Ishmaiah. Beyond these relationships, no other family connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Obadiah's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his role within the genealogical and tribal records of Israel. As the father of Ishmaiah and a member of the tribe of Zebulun, he contributes to the historical and tribal lineage important for understanding the organization of Israel during the period recorded in 1 Chronicles.
